frontmatter.title: QAOA: objective phases and mixing
frontmatter.description: The QAOA circuit family, an independently checked four-vertex MaxCut example, and full hybrid-workload accounting.

children.value: QAOA encodes a discrete objective in phases, then mixes computational-basis amplitudes so those phases can change the output probabilities

. A classical routine adjusts the phase and mixing angles. The quantum circuit supplies an objective distribution; finding useful angles, estimating that distribution, and returning a good assignment remain parts of the computation.
This page develops the QAOA example introduced in the

. Its four-vertex cycle is small enough to enumerate classically and to compare every ideal objective call with an independent formula. The example checks the implementation and this circuit family on the stated input. It supplies no general optimizer-convergence or quantum-advantage claim.

Recorded finite-shot resources: historical conditional model

This historical projection concerns the original one-layer C4 QAOA runs and their recorded 32-sweep sampled schedule. It does not estimate the larger inputs or the later depth-two compiled transcript. The

maps every initial call, incumbent remeasurement, accepted or rejected proposal, and holdout to an explicit measured circuit. The QAOA task has 473,856 preparations and 486 all-Z batches. These are modeled repetitions of stored circuits, not predictions of a fresh hardware-driven adaptive path.
These are the unchanged QAOA rows from the original replay, not a new estimate. Each task retains its separate whole-task physical-fault allowance
. The scalar is a coherent approximation-model quantity and is not summed over shots as a stochastic failure probability. Profiles retain physical error

Times sum every preparation’s model runtime; peaks take the maximum of independently selected class footprints. A common physical configuration is not verified. Physical initialization/reset, transport, routing, reconfiguration, communication and adaptive feedback remain unmeasured or excluded. The PSSPC rotation fit supplies expected resource cost, not concrete synthesized sequences, worst-case bounds, runtime-tail guarantees, or an output-accuracy certificate. CPU controller, reference and simulator times remain separate.

The larger shared size-study replay also retains all 72 runs and 5,859,840 preparations, including every quality miss. Its 84 cost classes and 85 searches remain a separate frozen record with independently selected class configurations. They are not a time-to-quality estimate or a physical proxy for the later initialization diagnostics, which have no new physical projection.

recorded a successful small QAOA trajectory, together with every query that preceded its final state. This replay asks a narrower implementation question: what happens when each of those fixed, bound circuits is routed and its arbitrary rotations are replaced by actual Clifford+T sequences? QAOA’s objective-dependent phase and mixer are explicit circuits
; neither the oracle construction nor the rejected optimizer work is an opaque free operation.
